subject: Snapshot handover protocol & attestation for private deployment - MSA/Order Form redlines
message_1_subject: Re: Snapshot handover protocol & attestation for private deployment
message_1_body:
Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're starting to pull the procurement paperwork together for the private deployment and Legal wants clarity on how Redwood will transfer and verify encrypted model snapshots if we exercise the on-prem delivery option in the Order Form. A few concrete asks: 

- Can you describe the handover protocol (file transfer + verification) for encrypted snapshots and any expected operator sign-offs?
- We need an attestation model: what evidence will Redwood provide that a snapshot was delivered, that keys were never copied, and that snapshots were deleted after transfer if requested?
- Are you open to a third-party attestor or a signed manifest approach instead of a full escrow?

I've attached a short requirements doc with the customer's minimum bar. Legal is specifically asking for: explicit audit window, manifest/hash verification, and a rollback test clause (we want to be able to verify a restore works in a controlled window).

Can you loop in whoever owns on-prem runbooks? We're trying to avoid long back-and-forth with procurement.

Thanks,
Rob Li
Infra Lead, CloudHealth Systems
infra-lead@cloudhealth.com

Attachment: cloudhealth_snapshot_requirements.docx (docx)
message_2_subject: Re: Snapshot handover protocol & attestation for private deployment
message_2_body:
Hi Rob — appreciate the clear asks and the doc. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Aditya (on-prem infra/runbooks).

High level options we recommend for customers:

1) Signed-manifest + HSM-based key exchange (preferred): we generate an immutable manifest with per-file SHA-256 hashes, sign the manifest with our code-signing key, and transfer the encrypted snapshot over SFTP or over your ingest pipeline. You (CloudHealth) validate the manifest and signature, and we provide a signed attestation PDF stating the transfer time, manifest hash, and key-handling summary. This avoids full-source escrow but gives cryptographic proof of receipt.

2) Escrow-lite with 3rd-party attestor: we engage a neutral attestor who will verify transfer and produce a notarized attestation; Redwood provides only the encrypted snapshot and a sealed hardware-backed key material statement. This is more operationally heavyweight but meets some compliance teams' expectations.

Action items from our side: we can prototype the signed-manifest flow and a rollback test (one-time restore verification in a dedicated staging window). I'll attach a draft addendum that maps to those two options and suggests language for the MSA/Order Form about frequency of audits and the restore test (one 48-hour test per quarter, optional).

Can you confirm which option Legal prefers and whether a 3rd-party attestor is acceptable? If so, share the attestor name or a short roster.

Thanks,
Kim
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_private_deploy_addendum_v1.1.docx (docx)
message_3_subject: RE: Snapshot handover protocol & attestation for private deployment — proposed redlines
message_3_body:
Rob / team — thanks for the requirements doc and context. From a legal perspective we've gone through Kimberly's draft and propose the following redlines (high level):

- License grant: limit to a deployment-only, non-transferrable runtime license tied to the Order Form. No implied rights to modify the model artifacts beyond what is required to restore runtime.
- Audit frequency and scope: agree to on-site or virtual audits no more than once per 6 months unless there is a breach or suspected misuse; audits will be scoped to transfer manifests, transfer logs, and the restore test window only.
- Attestation/escrow compromise: instead of full source escrow, Redwood will provide (a) signed manifest with per-file hashes and time-stamped signature, (b) HSM-backed key-handback statement, and (c) a third-party notarized attestation if requested by Customer and paid for by Customer. We will not provide private key material unless compelled by a court order.
- Restore verification: include a one-time 48-hour rollback verification per quarter (staging only) and a separate rollback exercise prior to go-live. Customer will provide a staging target and agreed rollback acceptance criteria.
- Data deletion: Redwood will provide a deletion report and hash-chain proof that a snapshot was removed from Redwood-managed transfer nodes within 7 business days of a deletion request.

I've uploaded a PDF with the specific redlined MSA excerpts (see attachment). Two small asks from your side: (1) confirm whether CloudHealth will accept the third-party attestor being chosen jointly (Redwood proposes a short list), and (2) whether procurement can accept the audit cadence as described.

Rishi Malhotra
Lead Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachment: msa_excerpt_redlines.pdf (pdf)
message_4_subject: Re: Snapshot handover protocol & attestation for private deployment — acceptance with minor edits
message_4_body:
Rishi / Kim — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. CloudHealth Legal is generally comfortable with the signed-manifest + HSM-backed statement approach. A few notes/questions before we finalize the Order Form: 

1) Please expand the restore acceptance criteria to include a basic integrity test (load model and run two sample inference queries) during the 48-hour rollback window.
2) We want the manifest signature to use an algorithm that we can independently validate (SHA-256 + RSA-3072 or ECDSA P-384).
3) For the third-party attestor option, procurement will cover the attestor fees but we need an estimated ballpark to include in the order form.

Procurement also asked for a link to the final redlined Order Form for routing. Can you send a DocuSign link when you're ready? We prefer to have the go-live rollback exercise scheduled within 30 days of signing.

I can confirm we accept the audit cadence if the scope is limited as proposed.

Thanks,
Meera Kapoor
Senior Counsel, CloudHealth Systems
legal@cloudhealth.com
